paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss Ratio FLOPs
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the loss ratio (in percentage) and the number of TeraFLOPs (TFLOPs) for different models, with the x-axis representing TFLOPs on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1e7 to 9e8 and the y-axis showing the loss ratio from 94% to 100%. The plot compares five models: Vanilla, SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=128), SepLLM (n=64, H), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T). The Vanilla model is represented by a purple line with triangle markers, showing a relatively stable loss ratio around 99.8% across all TFLOP values. The SepLLM (n=64) model, shown in orange with square markers, starts at approximately 98.1% loss ratio at 1e7 TFLOPs and increases to around 99.8% at 9e8 TFLOPs, with a peak near 100% at 4e8 TFLOPs. The SepLLM (n=128) model, depicted in blue with star markers, begins at about 97.2% loss ratio and rises to approximately 99.7% at 9e8 TFLOPs. The SepLLM (n=64, H) model, represented by a green line with diamond markers, starts at around 97.5% loss ratio and climbs to about 99.9% at 9e8 TFLOPs, peaking near 100% at 5e8 TFLOPs. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) model, shown in red with circle markers, starts at 94% loss ratio and increases to approximately 98.7% at 9e8 TFLOPs, with a peak around 99.2% at 3e8 TFLOPs. All models exhibit an increasing trend in loss ratio as the number of TFLOPs increases, with the SepLLM (n=64, H) model showing the highest loss ratio across most TFLOP values.
